pipeline.title: Collect public feedback
pipeline.what: Gathered Play Store reviews, Reddit posts and two complaint sites; only public pages, no logged-in Urban Company pages.

pipeline.title: Clean and de-duplicate
pipeline.what: Removed exact and near-exact duplicates, spam, professional-side posts and off-topic items; every removal is logged.
pipeline.numbers: 57 duplicates, 358 off-topic or out of scope removed

pipeline.title: Keep only traceable reviews
pipeline.what: A review is kept only if it has its own source URL, so every quote can be opened at its source.

pipeline.title: Label sentiment
pipeline.what: A word-list score gave a first label; unclear cases were read and corrected by the analyst (Claude). A random sample was re-checked.

pipeline.title: Code problems, behaviour and needs
pipeline.what: Phrase rules flag 26 problem and praise codes, return behaviour, alternatives and 14 unmet needs; the matched text was read and hand-curated.

pipeline.title: Check every quote
pipeline.what: Each quote shown on the site is tested to be word-for-word in the original review, with its source, URL and date.

pipeline.title: Score and rank opportunities
pipeline.what: Nine opportunities are scored on frequency, severity, evidence strength, repeat-booking relevance and an analyst impact judgement.

pipeline.title: Serve and explore
pipeline.what: The results are stored as JSON files, served by a read-only API and shown on this website.

negative_voice.title: Public posts over-represent bad experiences
facts: 44.1% of all reviews are Negative; 326 reviews come from complaint sites that are almost entirely Negative.
Google Play is 77.2% of the data and the only source with many positive reviews (45.6% Positive).
what_we_did: Added a further sample of detailed 4-5 star Google Play reviews, so that positive experiences carry real weight (Positive is now 35.4% of all reviews).
Showed sentiment per source instead of one blended mood, so complaint-site negativity is never read as the average customer.
Reported theme sizes two ways: pooled and with the four sources weighted equally, so a pattern that exists only on complaint sites is visible.
Kept positive reviews in every theme (T4 holds the praise as well as the failures) and compared returning with non-returning customers.
Read theme percentages as shares of the feedback, never as shares of all customers.

silent_churn.title: Customers who simply never came back leave no trace
facts: 86.8% of reviews (2,193 of 2,527) are placed as Return (1,119) or Non-Return (1,074); 13.2% stay Insufficient Evidence.
How each label was decided: 111 stated in the first person, 747 signalled (advising against the app, switching, distrust, or recommending), 1,335 inferred from sentiment and star rating.
what_we_did: Placed every review as Return, Non-Return or Insufficient Evidence, and recorded how it was decided (stated, signalled or inferred) and how sure we are.
Kept first-person statements and clear signals apart from sentiment-based inference, so the strongest evidence is never blended with the weakest.
Treated comparisons that use inferred labels as partly circular; the stated and signalled groups carry the findings.
Looked for loyal-but-unhappy customers: 39% of customers who say they came back are themselves Negative or Mixed.
Never reported a return rate: labels describe reviews, not all customers.
silent_churn.gap: Silent churners cannot be seen in public posts, so the true non-return share is probably higher than shown. The next step is first-party booking data: compare customers who rebooked within 90 days with those who did not, and run exit surveys.

sentiment.note: Agreement is between the word-list draft and the analyst's reading; it is not a human-labelled accuracy test.

quotes.note: Every quote is an exact extract of the original review text (whitespace aside).

urls.note: Every review links to its own page; the text of most was opened and matched against that page.

validation.rule_precision_note: Share of 6-8 randomly read matches per rule that really showed the issue. A spot-check, not a full accuracy test.

tests.covers: master dataset shape, quotes verbatim, every ID resolves, API contract, upload validation

golden_set.title: Golden set (hand-labelled comparison)
golden_set.note: A hand-labelled golden set, human agreement scores and accuracy tests belong to Step 3 and have not been run. No accuracy figure is claimed on this site.

limitations.coding: Issue, return, alternative and need flags are phrase rules, not a trained classifier; they can miss paraphrases and mis-fire on similar words. Measured precision (6-8 random matches per code): cancelled by the company or professional 88%, professional did not show up 88%, late or delayed 88%, no slots / professional unavailable 100%, prices too high or rising 88%, platform, visit and cancellation fees; policy rigidity 100%, extra charges and parts upselling 100%, support unreachable 75%, refund and payment problems 100%, complaint unresolved, no follow-up 88%, poor or incomplete work 88%, damage or theft 88%, rude conduct, safety, rating pressure 88%, trust, fraud or dishonesty 100%.
limitations.sentiment: Sentiment labels come from a lexicon draft plus analyst review of unclear cases (97% agreement on a 150-review check); they are not human-validated.
limitations.multi_label_counting: Theme counts overlap by design; do not add them.
limitations.small_groups: Only 111 reviews state return behaviour in the first person; household and discovery evidence are only a few dozen reviews. These are too small for statistical claims.
limitations.no_llm: These results were not produced by an LLM. An LLM backend (backend/) exists for the upload workflow and later steps.
limitations.not_validated: Step 3 (Golden Set, human labelling, accuracy and agreement) has not been run.
